artifacts.summary: Confirms the cross_batch defer-condition defect and root cause verbatim against the code, identifies the exact jq select() insertion point in orchestrate-batch-admit.sh's $hit computation, confirms in_batch is structurally unaffected, confirms exactly 3 files pin the v4 schema string, confirms zero regression risk but zero existing positive test coverage of the idle-cross-batch-overlap case, confirms the self-refuting rationale passage and the missing cross_batch Blocking-vs-Advisory row, and identifies the batch's sibling tasks (60, 61) and the four workaround-edge colliding tasks (53, 14, 17, 44) for the post-deploy CLOSING STEP.

memory_candidates.content: In this repo's orchestrate-batch-admit.sh, the collision-scan comparison-set construction and the per-candidate $hit selection are two separate jq stages: terminal/dependency-edge exclusion happens once when building $comparison_set, while the in_batch vs cross_batch directional/evidence test happens in the select() that computes $hit. A narrowing fix that must preserve in_batch behavior bit-for-bit while changing cross_batch behavior should add its new condition only inside the cross_batch disjunct of that select(), never touch the in_batch disjunct's existing $other_num < $c clause, and never touch $comparison_set construction (which is correctly the terminal/edge filter, not the evidence filter).

When narrowing a defer condition in a versioned NDJSON verdict schema in this codebase (orchestrate-batch-admit-v*), grep -rl '"<schema-string>"' across the extension root before estimating blast radius -- it reliably enumerates every file that must bump in lockstep (script emitter, schema doc, and any test asserting the literal $schema string), and cheaply confirms which sibling test files consume defer_reason/collision_scope only (no schema-string update needed).

This repo's batch-orchestration-guardrails.md Blocking-vs-Advisory criterion requires an advisory signal to still surface loudly, never silently -- when converting a formerly-blocking defer into an admit-with-advisory outcome, the established schema precedent to follow is self_modifying's shape (present on every verdict, never optional), not defer_reason's shape (present only on defer verdicts), because the new advisory condition fires precisely on the admit path where a defer_reason-shaped field would never be read.
